newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: U.N.'s Annan urges Albania rulers to show restraint.
newsitem.headline: U.N.'s Annan urges Albania rulers to show restraint.

text.p: U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan said on Tuesday he understood why people in Albania were angry and urged the government there to exercise restraint during the current unrest.
He also said the international community should provide financial aid if that would help stabilise the troubled Balkan nation.
Albania has been swept by violent unrest following the collapse of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes. The government declared a state of emergency and a nighttime curfew on Monday.

"I am rather disturbed by the developments in Albania and the confrontation between the government and the population. I hope the government will restrain itself and not use undue force against a people who feel legitimately aggrieved," he said.

Annan was speaking on the final day of a three-day trip to the Netherlands where he has met Dutch government leaders and top officials at the International Court of Justice and the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia.
Answering reporters' questions, Annan said it would be right for the outside world to contribute financial aid to Albania if that would help to stabilise the country.
"Obviously the whole genesis of the problem is financial, and if by offering financial assistance one can calm the situation, I think it's the right way to go," he said.

Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said the Netherlands, as current holder of the European Union presidency, was keeping close contact with other EU states about a coordinated response to the unrest in Albania, but he declined to disclose details.

"The situation in Albania is alarming...That is a reason for the Dutch presidency to do everything in the coming hours and days with the other member states to see how the European Union can help to find durable and effective solutions," he said.
